title: Stars: Red Giants and Helium Burning
welcome_lead: When the hydrogen runs low, stars swell and shine.
meta_desc: A-Level Astronomy: red giant phase, helium flash and shell burning.
final_note: Leaving the main sequence is the start of a star's dramatic life.

walkthroughs.body_html: When core hydrogen runs out, the core contracts and heats; hydrogen ignites in a shell. The outer envelope expands and cools, turning the star into a red giant.
In stars below about 2 solar masses, the helium core becomes degenerate. When it reaches 100 million K, helium ignites explosively — the helium flash — before regular core helium burning settles in.
Triple-alpha fuses 3 helium-4 nuclei into carbon-12. Further capture of helium can produce oxygen. The phase is shorter than hydrogen burning — helium fuel goes fast.

Its colour during its main sequence phase.
It is the hottest stage.
